S1-current: How to read protection: a line '# Vibe:' near the top means the file's own invariants are settling: their words may change without approval and a failing linked test only warns. '# Firm:' means their words wait for a signed approval, while a failing linked test only warns. No such line means solid: words wait for a signed approval and a failing linked test holds the commit. A word after one invariant's heading (firm or solid) raises that invariant to that level, whatever the file's line says.
S2-clause-vfs: How to read protection: HOLD says how an invariant is protected. vibe: its words may change without approval and a failing linked test only warns. firm: its words wait for a signed approval; a failing linked test only warns. solid: its words wait for a signed approval and a failing linked test holds the commit.
S3-word-draft: How to read protection: an invariant marked 'draft' after its heading is still settling: its words may change without approval and a failing linked test only warns. Without the word it is held: its words wait for a signed approval and a failing linked test holds the commit.
S4-clause-describes: How to read protection: HOLD says what is held. 'the words': the words wait for a signed approval. 'the tests': a failing linked test holds the commit. 'nothing yet': neither.
S5-word-three: How to read protection: a word after an invariant's heading. 'draft': its words may change without approval and a failing linked test only warns. 'agreed': its words wait for a signed approval; a failing linked test only warns. No word: held, its words wait for a signed approval and a failing linked test holds the commit.
